rounds.text: Thangamayil Jewellery Ltd is demonstrating exceptional fundamental momentum, backed by a rules-based screen scoring 85 out of 100 with a BUY rating [E65]. Compounded sales growth has accelerated significantly across all timeframes, hitting 83% over the trailing twelve months and 39% over three years [E16, E17], while profit growth has surged by 264% in the TTM and 64% over three years [E20, E21]. This top and bottom-line expansion is supported by elite capital efficiency, featuring an ROE of 28.1% and an ROCE of 25.5%, both vastly outperforming sector benchmarks [E9, E10, E12, E13]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is robust, reflected in positive money flow and increased holdings by foreign and domestic institutions up to 5.79% and 17.03% respectively [E41, E42, E43]. Operational execution remains strong with retail space exceeding 1,00,000 sq. ft, disciplined cost controls where retail revenue grew 28% against a mere 10% operating expense increase, and concrete expansion plans including new outlets and high-value product-mix targets [E78, E79, E81, E82]. Conceded: the stock trades at a rich valuation with a P/E of 38.5x and a price-to-book of 10.66x [E1, E2, E72], alongside a decrease in promoter holding over the last three years [E64].

The market is pricing Thangamayil Jewellery Ltd at a demanding valuation that leaves little margin for error, with a P/E ratio of 38.5x and a steep price-to-book ratio of 10.66x, significantly outpacing sector benchmarks [E1, E2, E7]. Underlying earnings quality shows cracks, highlighted by decelerating earnings growth flagged in the screening engines and an inconsistent quarterly and yearly operating margin trend [E33, E70]. Financial risks are mounting as total borrowings rose to Rs 913 Cr in March 2026 from Rs 797 Cr a year prior, accompanied by warnings that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E38, E63]. Insider confidence appears to be waning, demonstrated by promoter holdings dropping by 5.67 percentage points from December 2023 to September 2026 [E40]. Furthermore, management explicitly highlights a negative macro shift as younger populations pivot toward other discretionary spending [E84]. Conceded: the company displays strong historical compounding in sales and profits alongside an impressive institutional money flow and positive relative strength [E16, E21, E43, E50].

While the bear highlights a demanding P/E of 38.5x and P/B of 10.66x, these multiples are fully justified by elite returns on capital, with ROE reaching 28.1% and ROCE at 23.03%, vastly outperforming sector benchmarks where sector ROCE sits at a mere 10.27% [E1, E2, E10, E13]. Conceded: operating margins are flagged as inconsistent and earnings growth shows signs of deceleration in recent screens [E33, E70]. However, the business demonstrates phenomenal operating power, delivering a trailing twelve-month profit growth of 264% alongside ₹322 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹249 Cr in free cash flow for March 2026 [E21, E35, E36]. Conceded: borrowings increased to ₹913 Cr and promoter holdings decreased by 5.67 percentage points since December 2023 [E38, E40]. Yet institutional confidence is surging in the opposite direction, evidenced by foreign institutions increasing their stake by 5.05 percentage points and domestic institutions adding 5.63 percentage points over the same period, driving positive institutional money flow [E41, E42, E43]. Finally, the risk of younger demographics shifting discretionary spending is actively countered by management's strategic plans to improve high-value product-mix composition by up to 10% and expand operational retail space beyond 1,00,000 sq. ft [E79, E82, E84].

Conceded: the company delivers strong ROE and ROCE figures alongside significant operating and free cash flows [E10, E13, E35, E36]. However, the bull's justification of the 38.5x P/E and 10.66x P/B multiples ignores that these valuations vastly exceed sector benchmarks of 25.68x and 2.08x respectively [E1, E2, E6, E7]. While institutional accumulation and expansion plans are highlighted, borrowings have simultaneously expanded to ₹913 Cr and promoter holdings have declined by 5.67 percentage points [E38, E40, E41, E42, E48, E82]. Furthermore, the company faces documented risks of inconsistent operating margins, decelerating earnings growth, and an extraordinary shift among younger populations toward alternative discretionary spending [E32, E33, E70, E84]. The reliance on high-value product-mix targets to counter demographic shifts remains entirely speculative against a rich valuation that leaves a thin 5.2% margin of safety and a historical peak-to-trough drawdown risk of -66.3% [E45, E52, E72, E79].

Conceded: [E2], [E7], [E38], [E40], [E52]. The bear's concern over multiples and drawdowns ignores that premium valuations are justified by elite financial returns, with ROE at 28.1% and ROCE at 25.5%, vastly outperforming sector benchmarks of 8.65% and 10.27% [E9, E10, E12, E13]. While borrowings rose, they supported robust scaling that generated ₹322 Cr in operating cash flow and ₹249 Cr in free cash flow, proving the capital is productive [E35, E36, E38]. Furthermore, institutional confidence is accelerating rather than waning, evidenced by positive money flow and increased domestic and foreign institutional holdings [E41, E42, E43]. The worry about decelerating growth is countered by a massive 83% TTM sales growth and 264% TTM profit growth, alongside a rules-based screen scoring 85 out of 100 with a buy recommendation [E17, E21, E65]. Finally, management is actively defending margins through targeted cost optimization, which successfully kept operating expenses to a modest 10% increase against a 28% retail revenue growth [E81].

Conceded: [E35, E36]. While the bull highlights operating cash flow and free cash flow as proof of productive capital, the company's borrowings simultaneously surged to Rs 913 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 797 Cr a year earlier [E38], with explicit flags noting that the company might be capitalizing interest costs [E63]. The bull's reliance on institutional confidence and strong recent performance overlooks clear insider retreat, as promoter holdings have dropped to 61.65% from 67.32% [E40], marking a consistent multi-year decrease [E64]. Furthermore, the argument that premium multiples are justified by elite financial returns [E9, E10, E12, E13] ignores that the stock trades at an exorbitant 11.02x P/B against a sector benchmark of just 2.08x [E7], alongside an inconsistent annual operating margin trend over the last year [E32]. The rules-based screen cited by the bull explicitly flags that earnings growth is decelerating [E70], and the company faces an extraordinary shift among the younger population toward other discretionary spending [E84]. Finally, the worst peak-to-trough drawdown of -66.3% proves that these expensive valuations offer zero protection when market sentiment shifts [E52].
